name: Question 20
problem:
Express $\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)$ in the form $R\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x-ϕ)$ with $ϕ\in (0,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ Use the **exact value** for $R,$ and round $ϕ$ to **three decimal places**.

$\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)\,≈\,$
{{field-1}}
$\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x\,-$
{{field-2}}$)$
worked_solution:
The difference formula for cosine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)=R\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)=(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x).
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=4 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4} \\ ϕ & =arctan\,(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4})≈0.510\text{ }\text{rad},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2} & ={4}^{2}+(\sqrt{5})^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =16+5 \\ {R}^{2} & =21 \\ R & =\sqrt{21}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only consider the positive root since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)≈\sqrt{21}\,cos\,(6x-0.510).
$$
